author: cdc-rfc1-author (Claude Sonnet 5.5)
rationale: sticky_q <= sticky_q | fault_in_i is an exact same-direction q | independent_expression update with no reset, so the CDC-013 monotonic-level exemption applies and CDC-014 does not treat it as a toggle. The rest matches h23. Reader A's no-reset note is real but outside --deck cdc (RDC-025 excluded); adding a reset would remove the exemption. Class settled to Qualified payload and event protocols (Reader A) because the discriminating risk is the CDC-013/CDC-014 event-rate predicate, as in h10/h41.

author_reading.rationale: Monotonic sticky flag (only q | input updates, never cleared) feeds a clean two-stage synchronizer; a monotonic rise-only level cannot lose an event.

labels.rationale: The source has one direct rise-only sticky update, establishing the CDC-013 monotonic exemption. Two stages contain the crossing, and the output register and its synchronous reset share dst_clk.
labels.suspected_flaw: The prose implies a known power-cycle state for sticky_q, but the RTL has no reset or initializer to establish it.

labels.rationale: Source register sticky_q (src_clk, 20.0 ns) has a single rise-only monotonic update (sticky_q <= sticky_q | fault_in_i at design.sv:28) with no clear or reset, exempting it from CDC-013 and CDC-014, and crosses into dst_clk (8.0 ns) via a clean 2-stage synchronizer u_sync with complete boundary constraints.
